short_description: Moles, also called nevi, are pigmented skin spots that are usually harmless. However, they should be monitored for changes in size, shape, color, or bleeding.
temporary_advice: Take photos to compare changes over time
Protect skin from strong sun exposure
Use sunscreen when exposed to sunlight
Do not scratch or injure the mole
avoid: Do not try to remove a mole yourself
Do not ignore changes in size, shape, or color
Avoid strong sun exposure without protection
Avoid scratching or cutting the mole
risk_notes: Most moles are harmless, but changes in size, shape, color, border, or bleeding can be warning signs that require medical evaluation.
when_to_see_doctor: If the mole changes in size, shape, or color
If the mole has irregular borders
If the mole bleeds, hurts, or itches
If a new unusual dark spot appears
If the mole looks different from other moles
